decisive_items: a 15 cm mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall
a hysterectomy for micro-invasive cervical carcinoma in 2002
well-controlled HIV (viral load <40 copies/mL, CD4 count 290 cells/mm3)
response.rationale: A large mass arising from the vaginal wall in a woman with prior HPV-related cervical cancer and HIV immunosuppression most strongly supports a new primary vaginal carcinoma. Late recurrence of the original micro-invasive cervical cancer is less likely; lymphoma and GIST fit the vaginal-wall origin less well.

rejected.why: Systemic lymphoma is less consistent with the vaginal-wall origin and cecal fistulous connection; the elevated LDH and anemia are nonspecific.
GI lymphoma would better explain a cecal primary rather than a mass described as arising from the vaginal wall, and there were no GI symptoms.
GIST would not arise from the vaginal wall and mesenteric lymphadenopathy is atypical for GIST.
